name: es30-lighting
title: Lighting: directional, point, spot; Phong vs Blinn-Phong
summary: A lit 3D scene (checkered ground, spheres, boxes from procedural meshes, perspective camera) with ambient, directional, attenuated point and smooth-cone spot lights; Phong vs Blinn-Phong highlights, a correct vs a naive normal matrix on a non-uniformly scaled box, and per-vertex (Gouraud) vs per-fragment shading. Animated in windowed mode with keyboard control; validated against a CPU ray-cast evaluation of the same equations (analytic ground / sphere / box hits, exact barycentrics on the coarse mesh) in 70 per-object pixel sweeps and 86 further checks (named probes under isolated lights, matrix readbacks, defined errors, negative controls).
spec: ES 3.0 §2.12.6.1 Loading Uniform Variables In The Default Uniform Block (UniformMatrix{34}fv with transpose = FALSE, size/count INVALID_OPERATION cases, location -1 ignored)
ES 3.0 §6.1.12 Shader and Program Queries (GetUniformfv returns matrices in column-major order)
ES 3.0 §2.9 Vertex Arrays / §2.11 Vertex Array Objects (ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER binding is vertex-array state)
ES 3.0 §3.6.1 Basic Polygon Rasterization (front/back determination eq. 3.6, FrontFace, CullFace, perspective-correct interpolation eq. 3.7)
ES 3.0 §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point (8-bit result is one of the two closest values)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.5.1 Range and Precision (highp is IEEE single precision with the ULP table; pow inherits from exp2/log2), §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers
GLSL ES 3.00 §8.3 Common Functions (clamp, max, mix, mod, floor, smoothstep), §8.5 Geometric Functions (normalize, dot, length, reflect)

api.glGenVertexArrays: one VAO per mesh (ground grid, smooth sphere, coarse sphere, cube, cone); every drawn mesh matches the CPU geometry in the pixel sweeps
api.glBindVertexArray: VAO bound per draw; the index buffer is recorded in it and the draws still hit the CPU-predicted pixels
api.glGenBuffers: vertex and index buffer per mesh
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER and ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER (the latter bound while the VAO is bound)
api.glBufferData: interleaved position + normal floats and uint16 indices, observed through ray-cast pixel comparisons (positions) and lighting (normals)
api.glVertexAttribPointer: stride/offset of the interleaved layout, observed through geometry and lighting of every object
api.glDrawElements: TRIANGLES with UNSIGNED_SHORT indices from the VAO; 10 404 CPU-checked triangles; pixels of all objects match the CPU ray casts
api.glUseProgram: lighting program (per fragment) and Gouraud program (per vertex) selected per object
api.glGetUniformLocation: full names of struct members (u_material.albedo, u_spot.cos_inner, ...) resolve and the uploaded values reach the shader
api.glUniform1i: u_material.model selects Phong / Blinn-Phong: highlight probes match the matching CPU model and miss the other by >= 12 steps
api.glUniform1f: shininess, checker size, spot cone cosines: spot probes on the axis, in the falloff and outside the cone match to 1-2 steps
api.glUniform3f: light colours/positions/directions/attenuation, eye, material colours: all sweeps match; the attenuation negative control changes the result by 31 steps
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: u_model, u_view, u_proj with transpose = FALSE: read back column-major equal to the CPU matrices; the projected lamp centres land on the CPU-predicted pixels; the wrong-size call on a mat3 uniform is INVALID_OPERATION
api.glUniformMatrix3fv: u_normal_matrix = demo::math::normal_matrix(model): read back equal; crystal faces shaded as S^-1 R n predicts; the naive mat3(model) crystal matches the naive model and differs by 23 steps; count 2 on a non-array uniform is INVALID_OPERATION and leaves the value unchanged
api.glGetUniformfv: mat4 and mat3 uniforms of both programs read back bit-exact (column-major order, ES 3.0 6.1.12)
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST and CULL_FACE; with the ground drawn last the objects stay in front only because the depth test is on
api.glDisable: DEPTH_TEST negative control: the sphere pixel then shows the ground drawn later
api.glDepthFunc: LESS: reversed draw order sweep (all objects) still matches the CPU reference
api.glCullFace: BACK and FRONT: the upward ground is drawn or culled (clear colour) as predicted
api.glFrontFace: CCW and CW: the same four combinations; all 10 404 mesh triangles are CCW from outside
api.glClearColor: ray-through-nothing / culled pixels equal the clear colour
api.glClear: COLOR | DEPTH every frame; many consecutive frames in validate() all match their CPU reference
api.glViewport: full-surface viewport maps NDC to the CPU-projected pixels
api.glReadPixels: whole-frame RGBA8 readback for every configuration
api.glGetError: expect_gl_error(INVALID_OPERATION) after the two rejected matrix uploads; no error after location -1 uploads

visual_review.notes: Viewed gpu es-max and zink es-min captures (256x256, visually identical) plus 512x512 windowed/animated frames at t = 2, 5 and 8 s. Checkered slate-blue ground (finer and darker toward the top); back row two gold spheres (left blotchy faceted highlight = per-vertex, right smooth = per-fragment); middle row two teal stretched boxes, the right one (naive normal matrix) visibly darker on its left face; front row two red spheres, the right (Blinn-Phong) with a clearly larger soft highlight than the left (Phong). A warm orange pool with a small emissive lamp between the front and middle rows, a cool white spot pool with a soft edge on the floor to its left, a small pale cone (spot lamp) at the top edge. In animation the lamps move, the cone sweeps, the boxes rotate and the camera sways; xdotool key presses 2, 3, b, n, g, d turned the lights off, equalised the boxes and orbited the camera as documented.
